domain: On-device personal data stores (iOS 26 shipping / iOS 27 beta, July 2026) — EventKit, Contacts, PhotoKit, MediaPlayer, MusicKit, Files, Speech, JournalingSuggestions — for a self-installed personal quantified-self app on a FREE Apple ID

capabilities.stream: Calendar events (full read): title, start/end, all-day, status, availability, organizer, detached-instance flag, occurrence date, creation/last-modified dates
capabilities.api: EKEventStore.requestFullAccessToEvents(completion:) → EKEventStore.predicateForEvents(withStart:end:calendars:) → events(matching:) / enumerateEvents(matching:using:); objects are EKEvent : EKCalendarItem
capabilities.permission: System prompt "…would like to access your calendar" (Full Access variant). Info.plist key: NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 17.0 for the split API (framework itself iOS 4.0)
capabilities.resolution: Event-level; date range chosen by you. predicateForEvents expands recurrences into individual occurrences. No polling cadence — read on demand.
capabilities.backfill: Complete. Every event in every connected calendar, unlimited history and future. Note: some CalDAV/Exchange sources only sync a rolling window to the device, so "complete" means complete-as-synced.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE EKEvent properties (verified against Apple's full symbol index, not just the curated topic groups): eventIdentifier, availability (EKEventAvailability: .notSupported/.busy/.free/.tentative/.unavailable), startDate, endDate, isAllDay, occurrenceDate, isDetached, organizer (EKParticipant), status (EKEventStatus: .none/.confirmed/.tentative/.canceled), birthdayContactIdentifier, structuredLocation (EKStructuredLocation), birthdayPersonID [DEPRECATED], birthdayPersonUniqueID [DEPRECATED], refresh(), compareStartDate(with:). INHERITED from EKCalendarItem: calendarItemIdentifier, calendarItemExternalIdentifier, uuid, calendar, title, location, creationDate, lastModifiedDate, timeZone, url, hasNotes, notes, hasAttendees, attendees, hasAlarms, alarms, hasRecurrenceRules, recurrenceRules. || **`EKEvent.travelTime` DOES NOT EXIST.** The brief named it; I searched the entire EventKit symbol index for /travel/i and got zero hits across EKEvent, EKStructuredLocation, EKAlarm and EKCalendarItem. EKStructuredLocation has exactly three properties: title, geoLocation (CLLocation), radius (Double). The Calendar app's "Travel Time" field is not exposed publicly — treat it as unreadable. || EKAlarm: absoluteDate, relativeOffset, proximity (EKAlarmProximity .none/.enter/.leave), structuredLocation, type (EKAlarmType .display/.audio/.procedure/.email), emailAddress, soundName. || EKRecurrenceRule: calendarIdentifier, recurrenceEnd, frequency (.daily/.weekly/.monthly/.yearly), interval, firstDayOfTheWeek, daysOfTheWeek, daysOfTheMonth, daysOfTheYear, weeksOfTheYear, monthsOfTheYear, setPositions. || NON-OBVIOUS JOIN: birthdayContactIdentifier lets you join a Calendar birthday event straight to a CNContact across two separate stores.

capabilities.stream: Calendar attendees / participants: name, role, RSVP status, participant type — i.e. who you actually meet with, and how often
capabilities.permission: NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription (write-only access returns nothing here). Add NSContactsUsageDescription if you resolve participants to contacts.
capabilities.resolution: Per-event participant list. Attendee list is only populated for events from a server (Exchange/CalDAV/Google); a locally-created event usually has attendees == nil.
capabilities.backfill: Same as events — complete as synced.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE EKParticipant: isCurrentUser, name, participantRole (EKParticipantRole), participantStatus (EKParticipantStatus), participantType (EKParticipantType), url, contactPredicate, abRecord(with:)/abPerson(in:) [legacy]. EKParticipantScheduleStatus also exists as a type. || For a QS app this is the single highest-signal calendar stream: `attendees` + `startDate`/`endDate` gives you a real, dated social-interaction graph with duration — no other permission-only iOS API produces that. || Trap: EKParticipant exposes no email address directly on iOS; you must go through contactPredicate.

capabilities.stream: Calendar WRITE-ONLY mode (iOS 17+) — the negative case: what you get if you ask for the cheaper prompt
capabilities.permission: NSCalendarsWriteOnlyAccessUsageDescription — a visibly gentler prompt ("add events to your calendar")
capabilities.resolution: n/a — no read
capabilities.backfill: none
capabilities.notes: iOS 17 split the single legacy prompt into three. EKEventStore.requestAccess(to:completion:) is DEPRECATED. The three replacements: requestFullAccessToEvents, requestWriteOnlyAccessToEvents, requestFullAccessToReminders. Note the asymmetry — there is NO write-only variant for Reminders; reminders are all-or-nothing. || For a QS app write-only is useless: you cannot enumerate, query, or read back even events you created. Always request full access. Listed here so the distinction is explicit, because shipping the wrong Info.plist key silently yields an empty database and no error.

capabilities.stream: Reminders / tasks: completion state, completion date, due date, start date, priority — a free personal-productivity telemetry stream
capabilities.permission: NSRemindersFullAccessUsageDescription. Separate prompt and separate EKEntityType from calendars.
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 17.0 for the split API (EKReminder itself iOS 6.0)
capabilities.resolution: Per-reminder. completionDate is a full Date (timestamped to the second), not just a day.
capabilities.backfill: Complete for reminders still present in the database. **Trap: completed reminders are purged by the Reminders app over time**, so "complete history" is really "complete until Apple garbage-collects."
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE EKReminder: priority (Int), startDateComponents, dueDateComponents, isCompleted, completionDate — plus everything inherited from EKCalendarItem (title, notes, url, calendar, creationDate, lastModifiedDate, alarms, recurrenceRules, attendees, timeZone, location). EKReminderPriority enum: .none/.high/.medium/.low. || `completionDate` is the QS payload — it gives you a dated, timestamped record of task throughput with zero entitlement. predicateForCompletedReminders takes an explicit date range, so you can bucket by day/week directly in the query. || Note dueDateComponents is DateComponents, not Date — an all-day reminder has no time component and you must not force a timezone onto it.

capabilities.stream: Calendar structure: which accounts, which calendars, colors, types, subscription status — the metadata layer above events
capabilities.resolution: Static structure; changes rarely.
capabilities.backfill: Current state only — no history of calendar creation/deletion.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE EKCalendar: allowsContentModifications, cgColor, isImmutable, title, type (EKCalendarType: .local/.calDAV/.exchange/.subscription/.birthday), allowedEntityTypes (EKEntityMask), source (EKSource), isSubscribed, supportedEventAvailabilities (EKCalendarEventAvailabilityMask: .busy/.free/.tentative/.unavailable), calendarIdentifier. EXHAUSTIVE EKSource: sourceIdentifier, sourceType (EKSourceType: .local/.exchange/.calDAV/.mobileMe/.subscribed/.birthdays), title, calendars(for:). || Useful QS signal: EKCalendarType lets you separate work (.exchange) from personal (.local/.calDAV) automatically without asking the user to tag anything.

capabilities.stream: Calendar/Reminders change notification — know that something changed without polling
capabilities.resolution: Coarse — fires when the database changed. Carries NO payload describing what changed; you must re-fetch and diff yourself. Also invalidates your in-memory EKEvent objects (call refresh()).
capabilities.backfill: none — notification only, while your process is alive.
capabilities.notes: This is strictly weaker than Photos' and Contacts' change systems: EventKit has NO persistent change token and NO per-object change record. There is no EventKit equivalent of CNChangeHistoryFetchRequest or PHPersistentChangeToken. If your app is not running, changes are simply missed and you must reconcile by full re-fetch + your own snapshot diff. Design accordingly: keep your own last-seen table keyed by calendarItemIdentifier + lastModifiedDate.

capabilities.stream: Contacts: full contact records — names, phones, emails, addresses, birthdays, org/job, relations, social profiles, IM handles, photos
capabilities.entitlement: none — EXCEPT the note field (see separate row)
capabilities.resolution: Per-contact. You must declare keysToFetch up front; touching an unfetched key throws. Use CNContactFetchRequest + enumerateContacts for large stores — unifiedContacts loads everything into memory.
capabilities.backfill: Complete current state. NOT historical — a contact's edit history is not stored; see the change-history row.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE CNContact properties: identifier, contactType (CNContactType .person/.organization), namePrefix, givenName, middleName, familyName, previousFamilyName, nameSuffix, nickname, phoneticGivenName, phoneticMiddleName, phoneticFamilyName, jobTitle, departmentName, organizationName, phoneticOrganizationName, postalAddresses, emailAddresses, urlAddresses, phoneNumbers, socialProfiles, birthday, nonGregorianBirthday, dates, note, imageData, thumbnailImageData, imageDataAvailable, contactRelations, instantMessageAddresses. || EXHAUSTIVE key constants (these are what you pass to keysToFetch): CNContactIdentifierKey, CNContactTypeKey, CNContactPropertyAttribute, CNContactNamePrefixKey, CNContactGivenNameKey, CNContactMiddleNameKey, CNContactFamilyNameKey, CNContactPreviousFamilyNameKey, CNContactNameSuffixKey, CNContactNicknameKey, CNContactPhoneticGivenNameKey, CNContactPhoneticMiddleNameKey, CNContactPhoneticFamilyNameKey, CNContactJobTitleKey, CNContactDepartmentNameKey, CNContactOrganizationNameKey, CNContactPhoneticOrganizationNameKey, CNContactPostalAddressesKey, CNContactEmailAddressesKey, CNContactUrlAddressesKey, CNContactInstantMessageAddressesKey, CNContactPhoneNumbersKey, CNContactSocialProfilesKey, CNContactBirthdayKey, CNContactNonGregorianBirthdayKey, CNContactDatesKey, CNContactNoteKey (ENTITLED), CNContactImageDataKey, CNContactThumbnailImageDataKey, CNContactImageDataAvailableKey, CNContactRelationsKey, CNGroupNameKey, CNGroupIdentifierKey, CNContainerNameKey, CNContainerTypeKey, CNInstantMessageAddressServiceKey, CNInstantMessageAddressUsernameKey, CNSocialProfileServiceKey, CNSocialProfileURLStringKey, CNSocialProfileUsernameKey, CNSocialProfileUserIdentifierKey. || `CNContactStore.unifiedMeContactWithKeys(toFetch:)` returns the user's OWN "Me" card — free self-identification with no extra permission. || CNContactSortOrder: .none/.userDefault/.givenName/.familyName.

capabilities.stream: Contact NOTES field — the one Contacts datum behind a signed entitlement
capabilities.permission: NSContactsUsageDescription (same prompt as the rest — the user sees no extra prompt)
capabilities.entitlement: com.apple.developer.contacts.notes (Boolean YES). Without it, fetching CNContactNoteKey throws CNError.unauthorizedKeys.
capabilities.resolution: Per-contact free text.
capabilities.backfill: Complete current state.
capabilities.notes: CONTESTED / CONFLICTING SIGNALS — report both, don't pick a side. (a) Apple's entitlement doc says: "Add the entitlement to your app in the Xcode property list editor… **Before you submit an app with this entitlement to the App Store**, you need to get permission… Request permission at https://developer.apple.com/contact/request/contact-note-field" — which frames approval as an App-Store-submission gate, implying local dev/sideload works by just adding the key. (b) BUT "Contact Notes" does not appear ANYWHERE in Apple's Supported-capabilities (iOS) table, which is the authoritative list of what each membership tier can provision — including the free tier. Absence from that table means there is no free-tier provisioning row for it. || Practical read for a free Apple ID: try it; if the provisioning profile refuses the key, drop CNContactNoteKey from keysToFetch and lose only the notes field. Everything else in Contacts is unaffected. Failure mode is a thrown unauthorizedKeys error, not silent nil — so it is safe to attempt.

capabilities.stream: Contact groups and containers (accounts) — the social-grouping layer
capabilities.resolution: Group membership is a set; no timestamps on membership.
capabilities.backfill: Current membership only — but see change history, which DOES record add/remove-member events going forward.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE CNGroup: name, identifier, predicateForGroups(withIdentifiers:), predicateForGroupsInContainer(withIdentifier:), predicateForSubgroupsInGroup(withIdentifier:). Keys: CNGroupIdentifierKey, CNGroupNameKey. CNContainer keys: CNContainerNameKey, CNContainerTypeKey. || Container = the backing account (iCloud / Exchange / Local / CardDAV). defaultContainerIdentifier() tells you where new contacts go. Useful for separating work vs personal contact graphs the same way EKSourceType does for calendars.

capabilities.stream: Contacts CHANGE HISTORY — a genuine forward-looking event log of adds/updates/deletes and group membership changes
capabilities.api: CNChangeHistoryFetchRequest (set startingToken) → CNContactStore.enumerate…/execute via CNFetchResult<NSEnumerator>; persist CNFetchResult.currentHistoryToken; dispatch events through CNChangeHistoryEventVisitor
capabilities.resolution: One event object per discrete change. Events carry the changed object but NOT a timestamp — you timestamp them yourself at the moment you drain the queue, so your resolution equals your polling frequency.
capabilities.backfill: **NONE — this is the critical field.** History begins the moment you first persist a token (CNContactStore.currentHistoryToken). There is no retroactive window; you cannot ask "what changed last year." If your token ages out or the DB is rebuilt, the first event you receive is CNChangeHistoryDropEverythingEvent, which means "discard your mirror and re-sync from scratch." Take and store a token on very first launch, before you need it.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE event classes (all 12): CNChangeHistoryAddContactEvent, CNChangeHistoryUpdateContactEvent (.contact), CNChangeHistoryDeleteContactEvent, CNChangeHistoryAddGroupEvent, CNChangeHistoryUpdateGroupEvent, CNChangeHistoryDeleteGroupEvent, CNChangeHistoryAddMemberToGroupEvent, CNChangeHistoryRemoveMemberFromGroupEvent, CNChangeHistoryAddSubgroupToGroupEvent, CNChangeHistoryRemoveSubgroupFromGroupEvent, CNChangeHistoryDropEverythingEvent, plus the abstract base CNChangeHistoryEvent. Delivered via protocol CNChangeHistoryEventVisitor. || EXHAUSTIVE CNChangeHistoryFetchRequest config: startingToken (Data?), additionalContactKeyDescriptors, excludedTransactionAuthors ([String]?), includeGroupChanges (Bool), mutableObjects (Bool), shouldUnifyResults (Bool). || NON-OBVIOUS: `excludedTransactionAuthors` filters your OWN app's writes back out of the stream, so a QS app that also writes contacts doesn't feed on its own tail. Almost nobody uses this and it prevents a nasty feedback loop. || Also observe CNContactStoreDidChange notification to know when to drain.

capabilities.stream: Contacts LIMITED access mode (iOS 18+) — the partial-grant path most devs don't handle
capabilities.permission: NSContactsUsageDescription — the prompt now offers the user a third choice beyond Allow/Deny
capabilities.resolution: Only the user-selected subset of contacts is visible. Everything else behaves as if it does not exist.
capabilities.backfill: Complete history for the selected subset only.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE CNAuthorizationStatus: .notDetermined, .restricted, .denied, .authorized, .limited. || The failure mode is silent: under .limited your fetches succeed and return a small result set. If you only check `== .authorized` you will treat a partial grant as a denial; if you only check `!= .denied` you will report a partial contact graph as complete. Check for .limited explicitly and tell the user. || ContactAccessButton behaves differently per status: under .limited it shows matching contacts to add; under .denied it shows an allow-access prompt; under .authorized it renders nothing at all. || For a personal QS app the owner will just grant full access — but the code must still branch, because iOS may present the limited option by default.

capabilities.stream: Photos: per-asset metadata — creation date, added date, modification date, GPS location, media type/subtype, dimensions, duration, favorite, hidden, edited flag, source, burst identity
capabilities.permission: System prompt with Allow-All / Limited / Deny. Info.plist key: NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription
capabilities.resolution: Per-asset, second-level timestamps. `location` is full CLLocation (coordinate + altitude + horizontalAccuracy + timestamp + speed + course where captured).
capabilities.backfill: Complete — the entire library back to the first photo, including iCloud Photos assets not resident on device (metadata is local even when the pixel data is not). This is the deepest historical dataset available to a permission-only iOS app: for most people, a decade-plus of timestamped, geotagged life events.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE PHAsset properties: contentType (UTType), mediaType, mediaSubtypes, sourceType, pixelWidth, pixelHeight, addedDate, creationDate, modificationDate, location, duration, isFavorite, isHidden, hasAdjustments, adjustmentFormatIdentifier, adjustmentTimestamp, isSyncFailureHidden [DEPRECATED], playbackStyle, burstIdentifier, burstSelectionTypes, representsBurst, localIdentifier — plus iOS 27 beta: extendedMetadata, rating, originalResourceChoice, playbackVariation, adjustmentsState. || EXHAUSTIVE PHAssetMediaType: .unknown, .image, .video, .audio. || EXHAUSTIVE PHAssetMediaSubtype (12): .photoPanorama, .photoHDR, .photoScreenshot, .photoLive, .photoDepthEffect, .photoAnimation, .videoStreamed, .videoHighFrameRate, .videoTimelapse, .videoCinematic, .videoScreenRecording, .spatialMedia. **Screenshot detection = .photoScreenshot; screen-recording detection = .videoScreenRecording.** || EXHAUSTIVE PHAssetSourceType: .typeUserLibrary, .typeCloudShared, .typeiTunesSynced. || EXHAUSTIVE PHAsset.PlaybackStyle: .unsupported, .image, .imageAnimated, .livePhoto, .video, .videoLooping. || EXHAUSTIVE PHAssetBurstSelectionType: .autoPick, .userPick, .none. || `addedDate` (when it entered THIS device's library) vs `creationDate` (when the shutter fired) are different and both matter — a scanned old photo has a 1970 creationDate and a 2026 addedDate.

capabilities.stream: PHFetchOptions — the query gate that silently hides data if you don't set it
capabilities.api: PHFetchOptions passed to every PHAsset/PHAssetCollection fetch
capabilities.resolution: n/a — configuration
capabilities.backfill: n/a
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE PHFetchOptions: predicate, sortDescriptors, wantsIncrementalChangeDetails, fetchLimit, includeAllBurstAssets, includeHiddenAssets, includeAssetSourceTypes, prefetchAssetExtendedMetadata [iOS 27 beta]. || **THIS IS THE #1 SILENT-DATA-LOSS TRAP IN PHOTOKIT.** Defaults are exclusionary: `includeHiddenAssets` defaults to false (your "complete" library count silently omits the Hidden album), and `includeAllBurstAssets` defaults to false (a 20-shot burst appears as ONE asset). A QS app reporting "photos taken per day" will be quietly wrong on both counts unless it sets these. `includeAssetSourceTypes` similarly gates whether iCloud-Shared and iTunes-synced assets appear at all. || Set prefetchAssetExtendedMetadata = true on iOS 27 or you pay a separate fetch per asset when touching `extendedMetadata` — an N+1 across a 50k-asset library.

capabilities.stream: iOS 27 NEW — photo caption, original filename, keywords, and 1–5 star rating
capabilities.api: PHAsset.extendedMetadata → PHAssetExtendedMetadata { caption, originalFileName, keywords }; PHAsset.rating → PHAsset.Rating
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 27.0 (BETA as of July 2026 — GA expected ~Sept 14 2026)
capabilities.resolution: Per-asset. rating is a 6-case enum, not a float.
capabilities.backfill: Complete for any asset that carries the metadata; nil/empty where the user never set it.
capabilities.notes: VERIFIED iOS 27 beta via Apple's own symbol index beta flags (platform line reads "iOS 27.0 beta"), NOT from memory. Apple's human-readable PhotoKit "updates" page is stale — its most recent entry is June 2024 (spatial media) and does not mention any of this. || PHAsset.Rating cases (exhaustive): .unset, .one, .two, .three, .four, .five. || Companion write APIs also new-in-27: PHAssetChangeRequest.caption, .rating, .addKeyword(_:), .removeKeyword(_:). || `originalFileName` at the PHAsset level is new — previously you had to go through PHAssetResource to get it. || Also new in 27 for the picker: PHPickerMetadataOptions (.removeLocation, .removeCaptions) and PHPickerSearchText. || Contacts, EventKit, JournalingSuggestions and DeviceActivity have ZERO beta symbols in iOS 27 — they are unchanged. PhotoKit is where all the iOS 27 movement in this domain is.

capabilities.stream: Photo/video FILE-LEVEL facts: original filename, byte size, UTI, per-resource pixel dimensions, and which resources exist (original vs edited vs Live Photo video)
capabilities.resolution: Per-resource (an asset has 1..n resources).
capabilities.backfill: Complete.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE PHAssetResource: type, contentType (UTType), assetLocalIdentifier, uniformTypeIdentifier, originalFilename, pixelWidth, pixelHeight, dataSize [iOS 27 BETA]. || EXHAUSTIVE PHAssetResourceType (13): .photo, .video, .audio, .alternatePhoto, .fullSizePhoto, .fullSizeVideo, .adjustmentData, .adjustmentBasePhoto, .adjustmentBaseVideo, .pairedVideo, .fullSizePairedVideo, .adjustmentBasePairedVideo, .photoProxy. || **BIG PRACTICAL WIN IN iOS 27: `dataSize: Int?` is the first PUBLIC byte-size API.** For a decade the only way to get a file size was the private KVC hack `resource.value(forKey: "fileSize")` — undocumented, App-Store-rejectable, and liable to break. On iOS 27 you can compute real storage-consumption analytics legitimately. On iOS 26 and earlier your only *supported* option is to stream the resource through requestData and count bytes, which forces an iCloud download of every asset — impractical across a large library. This single addition is what makes a "where did my 200 GB go" feature viable. || Presence of .adjustmentData / .fullSizePhoto tells you the photo was edited and lets you distinguish original from rendered — that plus `adjustmentTimestamp` gives you an editing-behavior stream.

capabilities.stream: Full EXIF/TIFF/GPS/maker-note dictionary from the original image file (lens, aperture, ISO, shutter, focal length, camera model, orientation)
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 13.0 for requestImageDataAndOrientation (replaced the deprecated requestImageData)
capabilities.resolution: Full original-file metadata — everything the camera wrote.
capabilities.backfill: Complete, but see the iCloud caveat.
capabilities.notes: Set PHImageRequestOptions.isNetworkAccessAllowed = true or assets stored only in iCloud return nil with PHImageResultIsInCloudKey in the info dict — the single most common cause of "works on my device, empty in production." Also set .version = .original to read the camera's EXIF rather than the re-encoded edited render, and .deliveryMode = .highQualityFormat. || Read CFDictionary keys kCGImagePropertyExifDictionary, kCGImagePropertyGPSDictionary, kCGImagePropertyTIFFDictionary, kCGImagePropertyIPTCDictionary. || Cost warning: this pulls the FULL image bytes per asset. Across 50k assets that is both a huge iCloud download and heavy memory churn — batch it, throttle it, and cache results keyed by localIdentifier. Prefer PHAsset's cheap properties for anything they already cover (location, creationDate, dimensions) and reserve this path for lens/exposure data only PhotoKit doesn't surface.

capabilities.stream: Smart albums and user albums — Apple's own free classification of your library (screenshots, selfies, panoramas, bursts, slo-mo, RAW, favorites, hidden, recently-added, videos, spatial…)
capabilities.resolution: Collection membership; PHAssetCollection also exposes startDate/endDate/approximateLocation/localizedLocationNames.
capabilities.backfill: Complete.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE PHAssetCollectionSubtype — User albums: .albumRegular, .albumSyncedEvent, .albumSyncedFaces, .albumSyncedAlbum, .albumImported. Cloud: .albumMyPhotoStream, .albumCloudShared. Smart albums (21): .smartAlbumGeneric, .smartAlbumPanoramas, .smartAlbumVideos, .smartAlbumFavorites, .smartAlbumTimelapses, .smartAlbumAllHidden, .smartAlbumRecentlyAdded, .smartAlbumBursts, .smartAlbumSlomoVideos, .smartAlbumUserLibrary, .smartAlbumSelfPortraits, .smartAlbumScreenshots, .smartAlbumDepthEffect, .smartAlbumLivePhotos, .smartAlbumAnimated, .smartAlbumLongExposures, .smartAlbumUnableToUpload, .smartAlbumRAW, .smartAlbumCinematic, .smartAlbumScreenRecordings, .smartAlbumSpatial. Plus .any. || EXHAUSTIVE PHAssetCollectionType: .album, .smartAlbum, .moment. EXHAUSTIVE PHCollectionListSubtype: .momentListCluster, .momentListYear, .regularFolder, .rootFolder, .smartFolderEvents, .smartFolderFaces, .any. || EXHAUSTIVE PHAssetCollection metadata: assetCollectionType, assetCollectionSubtype, estimatedAssetCount, startDate, endDate, approximateLocation, localizedLocationNames. || .smartAlbumSelfPortraits is the free front-camera-usage stream. .smartAlbumScreenshots + .smartAlbumScreenRecordings are a decent proxy for "what was on my screen and when" given raw Screen Time is unavailable. || `estimatedAssetCount` can return NSNotFound — never display it without checking. || Moments (PHAssetCollectionType.moment / fetchMoments) are legacy: Apple stopped populating them when the Photos app moved to the Memories model, so treat moment fetches as likely-empty on modern iOS.

capabilities.stream: Live photo-library change observation — incremental inserts/deletes/updates/moves while your app runs
capabilities.api: PHPhotoLibrary.shared().register(_: PHPhotoLibraryChangeObserver) → photoLibraryDidChange(_: PHChange) → change.changeDetails(for:) → PHFetchResultChangeDetails / PHObjectChangeDetails
capabilities.resolution: Fine-grained: insertedObjects, removedObjects, changedObjects, hasMoves, plus index sets for animating a collection view.
capabilities.backfill: none — only while your process is alive and registered.
capabilities.notes: You must set PHFetchOptions.wantsIncrementalChangeDetails = true (and NOT set a fetchLimit) or hasIncrementalChanges is false and you get a coarse "reload everything" result instead of index deltas. || Callback arrives on an arbitrary background queue — hop to main before touching UI, and treat your old PHFetchResult as invalid the moment you receive PHChange. || Also register a PHPhotoLibraryAvailabilityObserver: the library can become unavailable (e.g. locked device / iCloud state) and PHPhotoLibrary.unavailabilityReason tells you why.

capabilities.stream: Photo-library PERSISTENT change history — catch up on everything that changed while your app was NOT running
capabilities.api: PHPhotoLibrary.currentChangeToken (persist it) → fetchPersistentChanges(since: PHPersistentChangeToken) → PHPersistentChangeFetchResult; iOS 27 adds PHPhotoLibraryPersistentChangesObserver
capabilities.resolution: Per-change records, enumerable in batches so a very large backlog doesn't blow memory.
capabilities.backfill: Forward-only from your first persisted token — same shape as Contacts change history. **But note the asymmetry: the underlying photo library itself IS fully historical, so a cold-start full fetch gives you all history; the token only saves you from re-scanning.** Tokens can expire; handle the error by falling back to a full re-fetch.
capabilities.notes: This is the correct architecture for a background QS collector: persist currentChangeToken at every sync, and on next launch drain only the delta instead of re-enumerating 50,000 assets. PHPersistentChangeFetchResult is explicitly designed to enumerate a very large change set lazily. || PHCloudIdentifier + cloudIdentifierMappings(forLocalIdentifiers:) / localIdentifierMappings(for:) let you keep a stable cross-device identity for an asset — localIdentifier is device-local and changes on restore, so a long-lived personal archive should store the cloud identifier.

capabilities.stream: Limited photo library mode — what a partial grant actually returns
capabilities.resolution: Only user-selected assets are visible. Smart-album and collection fetches return collections scoped to the selected set (typically near-empty).
capabilities.backfill: Complete history for the selected assets only.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE PHAuthorizationStatus: .notDetermined, .restricted, .denied, .limited, .authorized. EXHAUSTIVE PHAccessLevel: .addOnly, .readWrite. || Always call requestAuthorization(for: .readWrite) — the parameterless legacy requestAuthorization is deprecated and maps to a different level. || By default iOS re-prompts the user to update their limited selection once per app launch; set PHPhotoLibraryPreventAutomaticLimitedAccessAlert = true and drive it yourself via presentLimitedLibraryPicker, whose completion handler hands you the newly-selected localIdentifiers. || For a personal QS app the owner grants full access, so .limited is mainly a correctness branch — but it fails SILENTLY (fetches succeed, just tiny), so detect and surface it.

capabilities.stream: Photos with ZERO permission prompt — PHPickerViewController
capabilities.permission: NONE. No Info.plist key, no prompt, no authorization status. The picker runs out-of-process and hands back only what the user tapped.
capabilities.resolution: Per-selected-item. Initialize PHPickerConfiguration(photoLibrary:) if you need localIdentifiers back to re-join with PHAsset (that variant DOES require library authorization).
capabilities.backfill: none — user-driven selection only.
capabilities.notes: Worth stating because it's the cleanest permission story in iOS and people forget it exists: you can read arbitrary user-chosen photos with literally no permission prompt. Not useful for bulk QS telemetry, very useful for a manual "attach a photo to this journal entry" flow. || iOS 27 BETA adds PHPickerConfiguration.metadataOptions (PHPickerMetadataOptions: .removeLocation, .removeCaptions) — note the polarity: these STRIP metadata for privacy, they do not add any. Also new: PHPickerConfiguration.searchText / PHPickerSearchText to pre-seed the picker's search field.

capabilities.stream: Music library: every song in the library with play count, skip count, last-played date, 1–5 star rating, date added, genre, bookmark (resume) time
capabilities.permission: System prompt "…would like to access Apple Music" / media library. Info.plist key: NSAppleMusicUsageDescription
capabilities.resolution: Per-track LIFETIME COUNTERS — a single integer, not an event log.
capabilities.backfill: **"None" in the sense that matters.** playCount is a cumulative total with no per-play timestamps; lastPlayedDate is only the MOST RECENT play. You cannot reconstruct listening history — you can only snapshot the counters yourself on a schedule and diff them. Start snapshotting on day one or that history never exists.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE MPMediaItem properties: albumArtist, albumArtistPersistentID, albumPersistentID, albumTitle, albumTrackCount, albumTrackNumber, artist, artistPersistentID, artwork, assetURL, beatsPerMinute, bookmarkTime, isCloudItem, comments, isCompilation, isPreorder, composer, composerPersistentID, dateAdded, discCount, discNumber, isExplicitItem, genre, genrePersistentID, lastPlayedDate, lyrics, mediaType, persistentID, playCount, playbackDuration, playbackStoreID, podcastPersistentID, podcastTitle, hasProtectedAsset, rating, releaseDate, skipCount, title, userGrouping. || EXHAUSTIVE user-defined property keys (the QS-relevant ones): MPMediaItemPropertySkipCount, MPMediaItemPropertyRating, MPMediaItemPropertyLastPlayedDate, MPMediaItemPropertyUserGrouping, MPMediaItemPropertyBookmarkTime, MPMediaItemPropertyDateAdded. || EXHAUSTIVE filterable keys (usable in MPMediaPropertyPredicate): AlbumArtist, AlbumArtistPersistentID, AlbumPersistentID, AlbumTitle, Artist, ArtistPersistentID, Composer, ComposerPersistentID, Genre, GenrePersistentID, HasProtectedAsset, IsCompilation, **IsCloudItem**, MediaType, PersistentID, PlayCount, PodcastPersistentID, PodcastTitle, Title. || EXHAUSTIVE MPMediaType: .music, .podcast, .audioBook, .audioITunesU, .anyAudio, .movie, .tvShow, .videoPodcast, .musicVideo, .videoITunesU, .homeVideo, .anyVideo, .any. || **CONTESTED — is this still populated in the streaming era? Both sides:** FOR: Apple documents playCount, skipCount, rating and lastPlayedDate with no deprecation as of July 2026, and MPMediaItemPropertyPlayCount remains a *filterable* predicate key — you can build an NSPredicate on it, which would be odd for a dead field. AGAINST: multiple developer reports say counters do not update for cloud/streaming items, that assetURL is nil for Apple Music tracks, that playbackDuration can return 0 for iTunes/Apple Music tracks, and that isCloudItem is sometimes not set correctly on downloaded Apple Music tracks. **The discriminator is `isCloudItem`** — treat isCloudItem == true rows' counters as untrustworthy and isCloudItem == false (locally-owned files) as reliable. **Structural point that dominates both:** a pure stream you never added to your library never enters MPMediaQuery at all. MPMediaQuery reflects the *library*, so it only sees anything from Apple Music if the user has Sync Library enabled. For a modern streaming-only listener this API can legitimately return an almost-empty result — that is correct behavior, not a bug. Cross-check against MusicKit (next rows) rather than trusting either alone. || Separately: the 1–5 `rating` field is a LEGACY iTunes star rating, distinct from Apple Music's Love / Suggest-Less signals, which are NOT exposed by any public API. Expect rating to be 0 for essentially every modern user.

capabilities.stream: Currently-playing item from the system Music app (title/artist/album/genre + playback state, repeat/shuffle mode, queue index, volume)
capabilities.resolution: Event-driven via notifications while your app is alive; a poll otherwise.
capabilities.backfill: none — current state only.
capabilities.notes: **DIRECT ANSWER to "what can you see about currently-playing media from OTHER apps?": essentially nothing.** systemMusicPlayer reflects the Music app's state ONLY. Spotify, Overcast, YouTube, Podcasts etc. do not appear here. Apple's own doc even notes nowPlayingItem is nil if the user plays from another library via Home Sharing. || **MPNowPlayingInfoCenter is a WRITE API, not a read API.** MPNowPlayingInfoCenter.default().nowPlayingInfo is how YOUR app publishes its metadata to Control Center and the Lock Screen. You cannot use it to read another app's now-playing dictionary. (Its property key list is long — MPNowPlayingInfoPropertyElapsedPlaybackTime, …PlaybackRate, …MediaType, …AssetURL, …IsLiveStream, …ExternalContentIdentifier, …ExternalUserProfileIdentifier, …ServiceIdentifier, …PlaybackQueueCount, …PlaybackQueueIndex, …ChapterNumber, …ChapterCount, …CreditsStartTime, …AdTimeRanges, …CurrentPlaybackDate, …DefaultPlaybackRate, …AvailableLanguageOptions, …CurrentLanguageOptions, …ExcludeFromSuggestions, …InternationalStandardRecordingCode, …PlaybackProgress, MPNowPlayingInfoCollectionIdentifier, MPNowPlayingInfoProperty1x1AnimatedArtwork, MPNowPlayingInfoProperty3x4AnimatedArtwork — plus iOS 27 BETA MPNowPlayingInfoPropertyAppEntityIdentifiers — but they are all things you WRITE.) || The private MediaRemote framework (MRMediaRemoteGetNowPlayingInfo) is the well-known unsupported route. Do not plan around it: it is non-public API, Apple has repeatedly restricted its cross-process reach, and on a 7-day personal-team build you would be maintaining a reverse-engineered dependency that can break with any point release. || **The ONLY Apple-sanctioned read of third-party now-playing is JournalingSuggestion.GenericMedia — which is ADP-entitlement-gated and therefore unavailable on a free Apple ID.** See the JournalingSuggestions row and the blockers list.

capabilities.stream: Music library via MusicKit (modern replacement) — songs, albums, playlists, genres with playCount, lastPlayedDate, libraryAddedDate
capabilities.entitlement: none for library reads (see notes re: MusicKit App Service)
capabilities.resolution: Per-item; playCount is Int? and lastPlayedDate is Date? — both OPTIONAL, and the optionality is itself the signal that they are frequently absent.
capabilities.backfill: Counters are lifetime totals, same as MPMediaItem — no per-play log. libraryAddedDate gives you a real dated timeline of library growth.
capabilities.notes: EXHAUSTIVE MusicKit Song properties: id, title, artistName, artistURL, artists, albumTitle, albums, artwork, attribution, audioVariants, composerName, composers, contentRating, discNumber, duration, editorialNotes, endTime, startTime, genreNames, genres, hasLyrics, isAppleDigitalMaster, isrc, lastPlayedDate, libraryAddedDate, movementCount, movementName, movementNumber, musicVideos, playCount, playParameters, previewAssets, releaseDate, station, trackNumber, url, workName. || **This directly resolves half the contested play-count question: `Song.playCount: Int?` and `Song.lastPlayedDate: Date?` DO exist in MusicKit and are documented from iOS 16.0.** Older developer complaints that "playCount is not available in MusicKit" reflect the framework's initial iOS 15 state — note the Mac Catalyst 17.0 / macOS 14.0 availability line on these properties, which is the fingerprint of a later addition backfilled to iOS 16. Report both: the complaint was true historically, the property exists today. || Library request types available: MusicLibraryRequest, MusicLibrarySearchRequest, MusicLibrarySectionedRequest, plus filter/sort protocols LibrarySongFilter, LibrarySongSortProperties, LibraryAlbumFilter/SortProperties, LibraryArtistFilter/SortProperties, LibraryGenreFilter/SortProperties, LibraryPlaylistFilter/SortProperties, LibraryPlaylistEntryFilter/SortProperties, LibraryMusicVideoFilter/SortProperties, LibraryTrackFilter/SortProperties. || CAVEAT TO VERIFY ON DEVICE: Apple's "Using Automatic Developer Token Generation for Apple Music API" requires enabling the **MusicKit App Service** on your App ID in the developer portal. Local *library* requests are widely reported to work without it; anything hitting the Apple Music *catalog* (MusicCatalogSearchRequest, MusicPersonalRecommendationsRequest, and plausibly MusicRecentlyPlayedRequest) needs a developer token. On a free Apple ID you cannot configure App Services on an App ID, so budget for catalog requests failing and library requests succeeding — test this early, it is the one item in this domain I could not settle from documentation alone.

capabilities.stream: Recently-played items (albums / playlists / stations) and personal recommendations
capabilities.entitlement: none locally, but see the MusicKit App Service / developer-token caveat
capabilities.resolution: An ordered recency list, not timestamped plays.
capabilities.backfill: **A short rolling window only** — commonly ~25 items by default; `limit` bounds it. This is a "what am I listening to lately" surface, not a history API. Snapshot it repeatedly and diff if you want a timeline.
capabilities.notes: RecentlyPlayedMusicItem enum covers album / playlist / station. MusicPersonalRecommendation + MusicPersonalRecommendationsRequest expose Apple's own recommendations derived from the user's listening — an indirect but real read on taste. || MusicSubscription tells you whether the user has an active Apple Music subscription and can play catalog content, which is how you decide at runtime whether the MediaPlayer path or the MusicKit path will have data.

capabilities.stream: Apple Music capabilities / storefront (LEGACY — do not build on this)
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 9.3 — **DEPRECATED in iOS 18.0** (entire class, all methods)
capabilities.resolution: Capability bitmask + storefront country code.
capabilities.backfill: none
capabilities.notes: The brief named SKCloudServiceController; flagging that it is DEPRECATED as of iOS 18.0 across every platform (macOS 15.0, watchOS 11.0, tvOS 18.0). It still functions on iOS 26/27 but should not be designed around. Replacements: MusicAuthorization.request() for consent, MusicSubscription.current for capability/subscription state. Notifications SKCloudServiceCapabilitiesDidChange, SKStorefrontCountryCodeDidChange, SKStorefrontIdentifierDidChange are deprecated with it.

capabilities.stream: Arbitrary user files and whole folder trees (Files.app / iCloud Drive / external drives) — persistently, across launches
capabilities.api: UIDocumentPickerViewController(forOpeningContentTypes: [.folder]) → delegate URL → url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() → FileManager enumeration → url.bookmarkData(options: .minimalBookmark) persisted → URL(resolvingBookmarkData:bookmarkDataIsStale:)
capabilities.permission: **NONE.** No Info.plist usage-description key and no runtime permission dialog. The user's act of picking IS the grant.
capabilities.resolution: Full filesystem access to the granted subtree: file contents, sizes, creation/modification dates, extended attributes.
capabilities.backfill: Complete for whatever the user grants, and it PERSISTS — a security-scoped bookmark survives app relaunch and device reboot.
capabilities.notes: **This is the strongest and most under-used capability in the whole domain, and the only "read arbitrary user data" surface on iOS with ZERO permission prompt and ZERO entitlement.** Pick a folder once, bookmark it, and you have a durable, re-openable window into a real directory tree — perfect for a personal QS app ingesting exports, CSVs, backups, or Obsidian-style note vaults. || Discipline: always balance startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() with stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() (there is a hard limit on concurrently-open scopes), and handle bookmarkDataIsStale by re-resolving and re-saving. Without startAccessing… every read fails with a permission error even though you hold a valid URL — that is the classic first-time bug. || Use NSFileCoordinator/NSFilePresenter for anything in iCloud Drive to avoid racing the sync daemon. || Init with `forOpeningContentTypes: [.folder]` for tree access; `asCopy: false` to get the live URL rather than a snapshot copy into your tmp dir.

capabilities.stream: FileProvider — the inverse direction (vending, not reading)
capabilities.api: NSFileProviderExtension / replicated or nonreplicated File Provider extension; NSFileProviderManager, NSFileProviderDomain, NSFileProviderItem
capabilities.entitlement: No signed entitlement to build one; "FileProvider Testing Mode" is a separate capability and is ADP/ADEP-only, development-only.
capabilities.resolution: n/a
capabilities.backfill: n/a
capabilities.notes: CLARIFYING A COMMON MISREADING: FileProvider lets YOUR app publish its files INTO the Files app for other apps to browse. It does **not** let you read files belonging to Dropbox, Google Drive, or any other provider. For a QS app that is the wrong tool — UIDocumentPickerViewController (previous row) is the tool. || Included because the brief named it and because the natural assumption ("FileProvider = read the Files app") is backwards; getting this wrong costs a wasted build cycle. || Related: NSMetadataQuery over ubiquitous (iCloud) scopes requires the iCloud capability, which Apple's supported-capabilities table shows is NOT available to the free tier — so iCloud-Drive-wide indexing is out on a free Apple ID, while picker+bookmark access to the same files is in.

capabilities.stream: Speech-to-text over recorded audio FILES (voice memos, interviews, your own ambient recordings) and live microphone
capabilities.api: SFSpeechRecognizer.requestAuthorization → SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest(url:) for files, or SFSpeechAudioBufferRecognitionRequest for live audio → recognitionTask(with:resultHandler:)
capabilities.permission: Two prompts: NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription (always) and NSMicrophoneUsageDescription (only for live capture — NOT needed for file transcription)
capabilities.resolution: Word-level with per-segment timestamps, duration, and confidence; alternative interpretations via transcriptions[].
capabilities.backfill: Complete for any audio file you can reach — so pairing this with the document-picker row lets you transcribe an entire archive of recordings with no entitlement at all.
capabilities.notes: Check `supportsOnDeviceRecognition` and set request.requiresOnDeviceRecognition = true to keep audio off Apple's servers — for a personal QS app that is the correct default, and it also removes the ~1 minute duration cap and the network dependency that server-side recognition imposes. || `isAvailable` can be false transiently; observe SFSpeechRecognizerDelegate. || SFSpeechLanguageModel / SFCustomLanguageModelData let you bias recognition toward your own vocabulary (names, jargon) — a real accuracy win on personal recordings. || supportedLocales() enumerates what's installable.

capabilities.stream: Speech, modern path — SpeechAnalyzer / SpeechTranscriber / DictationTranscriber / SpeechDetector (voice-activity detection)
capabilities.api: actor SpeechAnalyzer + modules SpeechTranscriber, DictationTranscriber, SpeechDetector; AssetInventory / AssetInstallationRequest for model management; AnalyzerInput; AssetInputSequenceProvider / CaptureInputSequenceProvider / AnalyzerInputConverter
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 26.0 for SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber; the input-provider and converter classes are iOS 27.0 BETA
capabilities.resolution: Streaming, long-form, on-device. Substantially better than SFSpeechRecognizer for extended audio.
capabilities.backfill: Complete over any reachable audio.
capabilities.notes: iOS 26 introduced the SpeechAnalyzer architecture ALONGSIDE the legacy SFSpeechRecognizer (which is not deprecated) — they are separate stacks with different minimum OS versions, so keep both paths if you support iOS 25 or earlier. || VERIFIED iOS 27 BETA additions (from Apple's beta symbol flags, dated June 2026 on the Speech updates page): AssetInputSequenceProvider (read from an AVAsset/file), CaptureInputSequenceProvider (read from an AVCaptureDevice/microphone), AnalyzerInputConverter (convert AVAudioBuffer → AnalyzerInput), AnalyzerInput.bufferDuration / .bufferFormat, SpeechAnalyzer.Options.ignoresResourceLimits, SFSpeechError.Code.cannotConfigureAudioSystem. These remove most of the audio-plumbing boilerplate that iOS 26 required. || **SpeechDetector is the sleeper QS primitive:** pure voice-activity detection means you can measure *how much you spoke* and when, without transcribing or storing a single word — a privacy-preserving conversation-volume metric. || AssetInventory / SpeechModels: transcription models are downloaded per-locale, so handle the not-yet-installed state on first run.

capabilities.stream: Journaling Suggestions — Apple's curated cross-domain feed (photos, locations visited, workouts, motion/steps, songs, podcasts, THIRD-PARTY now-playing, contacts interacted with, State of Mind, event posters)
capabilities.api: JournalingSuggestionsPicker → JournalingSuggestion → suggestion.content(forType:) for each of the 15 item types; JournalingSuggestionsConfiguration + JournalingSuggestionPresentationToken for system notifications
capabilities.permission: No Info.plist usage string. Consent is the picker itself — the user explicitly taps each suggestion they want to hand over. Nothing is readable without an affirmative per-item selection.
capabilities.entitlement: **com.apple.developer.journal.allow — REQUIRED, and it is ADP (paid Apple Developer Program) ONLY.** Apple's Supported-capabilities (iOS) table lists Journaling Suggestions with a check in the ADP column and NO check in the free "Apple Developer" column. Without the entitlement in your code signature the framework refuses to present the picker at all.
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 17.2; **iPadOS 26.0** (iPad support was added in iPadOS 26); physical devices only, not Simulator
capabilities.resolution: Per-suggestion, each carrying its own date/DateInterval. Media assets arrive as file URLs on disk.
capabilities.backfill: A short recent window — these are "recent, personal events" surfaced for journaling, not a queryable history. There is no way to ask for last year.
capabilities.notes: **LEAD WITH THE BLOCKER: this entire framework is unavailable on a free Apple ID.** I verified this by parsing Apple's supported-capabilities table's raw HTML rather than trusting a page summary — a text summarizer read the row inverted and reported it as free-tier-available. It is not. || EXHAUSTIVE — all 15 JournalingSuggestion item types with every field: **Contact** (name, photo URL). **Photo** (photo URL, date). **LivePhoto** (image URL, video URL, date). **Video** (url, date). **Song** (song, artist, album, artwork URL, date). **Podcast** (show, episode, artwork URL, date). **GenericMedia** [iOS 18] (title, artist, album, date, appIcon URL). **Location** (city, place, location CLLocation, date, isWorkLocation, mapKitItemIdentifier). **LocationGroup** (locations: [Location]). **Workout** (icon URL, route: [CLLocation], details: Workout.Details, localizedName). **WorkoutGroup** (icon, duration, activeEnergyBurned HKQuantity, averageHeartRate HKQuantity, workouts: [Workout]). **MotionActivity** (icon, date DateInterval, steps Int, movementType MovementType). **StateOfMind** [iOS 18] (state HKStateOfMind, icon, lightBackground/darkBackground Gradient). **Reflection** [iOS 18] (prompt, color). **EventPoster** [iOS 26] (title AttributedString, placeName, image URL, eventStart, eventEnd, isHost). Top-level JournalingSuggestion carries: title, date (DateInterval?), items ([ItemContent]). || **GenericMedia is the single most valuable row in this table and the reason the blocker stings:** Apple's iOS 26 release notes say it collects "asset content that includes other media playback sessions from other music or podcast Apps," and its `appIcon` is documented as "the Now Playing app that played the media item." That is the ONLY sanctioned way an iOS app can learn what a THIRD-PARTY app (Spotify, Overcast) was playing — and it sits behind a paid-tier entitlement. || iOS 26 also added: system notifications (JournalingSuggestionsConfiguration + JournalingSuggestionPresentationToken) that prompt the user to reflect and deep-link into your picker; Location.isWorkLocation and .mapKitItemIdentifier; Workout.localizedName; landscape support; MotionActivity.MovementType (run vs mixed run/walk sessions).

blockers: **7-DAY PROVISIONING EXPIRY — the one that actually decides this project.** A free Apple ID gives you a "Personal Team" whose provisioning profiles expire 7 days after creation. When the profile expires the app STOPS LAUNCHING until you rebuild and redeploy from Xcode. For a quantified-self app whose entire value is continuous, unattended collection, this is fatal independent of any API question: every 7 days the data stream dies until you plug in a Mac. Related personal-team limits: App IDs capped at 10 (each expiring in 7 days) and registered devices capped at 3 per platform. **Mitigation to price against: the $99/yr Apple Developer Program raises the profile lifetime to 1 year and unlocks every entitlement below.** Realistically, $99 is the correct answer for this project — a year of uninterrupted collection plus JournalingSuggestions plus Family Controls, versus a weekly manual re-sign ritual and a permanently truncated feature set.

**JournalingSuggestions is entirely unavailable on a free Apple ID.** com.apple.developer.journal.allow appears in the ADP (paid) column of Apple's Supported-capabilities (iOS) table with NO check in the free "Apple Developer" column. Without the entitlement in the code signature the framework refuses to present JournalingSuggestionsPicker at all — there is no degraded mode. This costs you all 15 suggestion types, and specifically costs you `JournalingSuggestion.GenericMedia`, which is the ONLY Apple-sanctioned surface for reading what a THIRD-PARTY media app (Spotify, Overcast, YouTube) was playing. VERIFICATION NOTE: I parsed the capability table's raw HTML directly because an automated page summary reported this row INVERTED (claimed free-tier availability). Do not trust secondary summaries of that table.

**Family Controls / Screen Time is doubly blocked.** com.apple.developer.family-controls is listed ADP-only AND flagged "(development)" — development-only even for paid members, with distribution requiring a separate manual capability request that Apple reviews and approves case-by-case. On a free Apple ID you cannot call AuthorizationCenter.requestAuthorization at all, so DeviceActivity, ManagedSettings and every Screen Time API are simply absent.

**Even WITH the Family Controls entitlement, Screen Time data cannot leave the extension.** The DeviceActivityReport extension is sandboxed such that it can make no network requests and cannot read or write App Group shared containers — the app and extension get separate stores despite an identical suiteName. Apple DTS states plainly that moving Device Activity data outside the extension's sandbox is not possible, by design, to preserve privacy. The extension can RENDER a report SwiftUI view; it can never hand you a number. This is a harder blocker than the entitlement itself and is the item most often gotten wrong in planning — people budget for the entitlement, get it, and then discover the data is unexportable.

**Contact notes (CNContactNoteKey) — conflicting signals, expect failure.** The entitlement doc frames approval as an App-Store-SUBMISSION gate (implying local builds work by just adding the Boolean key), but "Contact Notes" does not appear ANYWHERE in Apple's Supported-capabilities (iOS) table — including the free-tier column — which means there is no provisioning row for it at any membership level without the manual request at developer.apple.com/contact/request/contact-note-field. I am reporting the conflict rather than picking a side. Practical impact is small and the failure is loud: fetching CNContactNoteKey without the entitlement throws CNError.unauthorizedKeys, so attempt it, catch, and drop that one key.

**`EKEvent.travelTime` does not exist.** The brief named it as a readable EventKit property. I searched Apple's complete EventKit symbol index for /travel/i and got zero hits across EKEvent, EKCalendarItem, EKStructuredLocation and EKAlarm. EKStructuredLocation has exactly three properties (title, geoLocation, radius). The Calendar app's Travel Time field is real but has no public API — plan without it.

**iCloud/CloudKit, Push Notifications, Siri/SiriKit, Sign in with Apple, Communication Notifications, Associated Domains, Network Extensions, NFC and App Attest are all unavailable on the free tier** per the same capability table. Practical consequences for a QS app: no CloudKit sync/backup across your own devices, no server-triggered wake, no Siri Shortcuts donation, and no iCloud-Drive-wide NSMetadataQuery indexing. Notably AVAILABLE on the free tier: App Groups, Background Modes, HealthKit, HomeKit, Keychain Sharing, Data Protection, Maps. App Groups being free-tier is worth flagging because it is widely (and incorrectly) reported as paid-only — Apple's own table checks the free column, though scattered forum reports describe provisioning errors, so verify on device before designing around it.
nonObvious: **Apple's rendered documentation is JS-only, but there is a stable JSON API behind it — and a separate index endpoint that flags beta symbols.** `https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/<path>.json` returns the full symbol payload; `https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/index/<framework>.json` returns the whole symbol tree with per-node `beta` and `deprecated` flags. Walking the index for beta flags is how I found every iOS 27 addition in this domain in one pass. This matters because **Apple's human-readable "updates" pages are stale**: the PhotoKit updates page's most recent entry is June 2024 (spatial media) and mentions none of the iOS 27 work. Anyone reading the updates page would conclude PhotoKit is unchanged. It is the framework with the most iOS 27 movement in this entire domain.

**`topicSections` in Apple's docs are CURATED groupings, not exhaustive member lists** — Apple routinely omits symbols from them. Any enumeration built from the rendered page's section headings is silently incomplete. Build from the index tree instead, then diff. (I did this for EKEvent, EKStructuredLocation, CNContact, PHAsset, PHAssetResource and MPMediaItem; they happened to agree, but the method is what makes the negative claims — especially "travelTime does not exist" — actually auditable rather than an absence of evidence.)

**PHFetchOptions defaults hide data, silently.** `includeHiddenAssets` defaults to false, so your "complete" library enumeration omits the entire Hidden album. `includeAllBurstAssets` defaults to false, so a 20-shot burst counts as ONE asset. `includeAssetSourceTypes` gates whether iCloud-Shared and iTunes-synced assets appear at all. A photos-per-day metric is wrong on all three counts by default, with no error and no warning. This is the single highest-frequency correctness bug in PhotoKit work.

**iOS 27 finally makes photo file sizes legal.** `PHAssetResource.dataSize: Int?` is new in the iOS 27 beta. For a decade the only way to get a photo's byte size was the private KVC hack `resource.value(forKey: "fileSize")` — undocumented and rejectable — because the only supported alternative was streaming every resource through PHAssetResourceManager.requestData and counting bytes, which forces an iCloud download of the entire library. A legitimate 'where did my 200 GB go' feature was effectively impossible before iOS 27 and is trivial after.

**`isCloudItem` is a FILTERABLE predicate key, which makes it the programmatic discriminator for the whole play-count controversy.** Because MPMediaItemPropertyIsCloudItem can be used in an MPMediaPropertyPredicate, you can partition the library server-side-of-the-API into locally-owned files (counters trustworthy) and cloud/Apple Music items (counters unreliable per widespread developer reports) rather than arguing about it. The deeper structural point most people miss: a pure stream never added to the library never enters MPMediaQuery AT ALL — MPMediaQuery reflects the *library*, so it only sees Apple Music content when Sync Library is on. An empty result for a modern streaming-only listener is correct behavior, not a bug.

**`EKEvent.birthdayContactIdentifier` is a free cross-store join key** — it links a Calendar birthday event directly to a CNContact identifier, letting you fuse the calendar graph and the contact graph across two separate permission domains with no fuzzy name matching.

**`CNChangeHistoryFetchRequest.excludedTransactionAuthors` filters your OWN app's writes back out of the change stream.** Almost nobody uses it. If your QS app both reads and writes contacts, omitting this creates a feedback loop where the app perpetually re-processes its own edits.

**Change-history tokens are forward-only and must be taken on FIRST launch, before you need them.** Contacts (CNContactStore.currentHistoryToken) and Photos (PHPhotoLibrary.currentChangeToken) both begin history at the moment you first persist a token — there is no retroactive window, ever. The asymmetry worth knowing: the Photos *library* is itself fully historical, so a cold full fetch recovers everything and the token is only an optimization; **Contacts change history is the sole record of contact mutation and is irrecoverable if you didn't start it.** `CNChangeHistoryDropEverythingEvent` is the signal your token aged out and you must resync from scratch. **EventKit has NO change token at all** — only a payload-free EventStoreChanged notification, so calendar sync requires your own snapshot-and-diff against calendarItemIdentifier + lastModifiedDate.

**`SpeechDetector` (iOS 26) does voice-activity detection WITHOUT transcription** — you can measure how much you spoke and when without capturing or storing a single word. That is a genuinely privacy-preserving conversation-volume metric, and it's the kind of thing a QS app should prefer over full transcription by default.

**UIDocumentPickerViewController + a security-scoped bookmark is the only zero-permission, zero-entitlement, PERSISTENT arbitrary-file-read on iOS.** No Info.plist string, no prompt, no authorization status — the user's act of picking is the grant, and the bookmark survives relaunch and reboot. Pick a folder with `forOpeningContentTypes: [.folder]` and you hold a durable window into a whole directory tree. The universal first-time bug: you must call `startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()` before every access or reads fail with permission errors despite holding a valid URL — and you must balance it with `stopAccessing…` because concurrently-open scopes are hard-capped.

**FileProvider is backwards from what everyone assumes.** It lets your app VEND files INTO the Files app; it does not let you READ Dropbox's or Google Drive's files. Assuming otherwise costs a wasted build cycle. The document picker is the tool for reading.

**MPNowPlayingInfoCenter is a WRITE API.** Its ~25 property keys are things your app PUBLISHES to Control Center and the Lock Screen — it is not a window into other apps' playback, and the naming misleads consistently. Combined with systemMusicPlayer reflecting only the Music app, the honest conclusion is that third-party now-playing is unreadable except through the ADP-gated JournalingSuggestion.GenericMedia.

**iOS 18 added `.limited` to Contacts, matching what Photos got in iOS 14 — and both fail SILENTLY.** Under a limited grant your fetches SUCCEED and return a small result set. Code that checks only `== .authorized` misreads a partial grant as denial; code that checks only `!= .denied` reports a partial graph as complete. Both frameworks provide UI to expand the grant (ContactAccessButton / .contactAccessPicker; presentLimitedLibraryPicker) and both let you suppress the automatic re-prompt (PHPhotoLibraryPreventAutomaticLimitedAccessAlert).

**`PHAsset.addedDate` and `PHAsset.creationDate` are different and both matter.** creationDate is when the shutter fired; addedDate is when the asset entered THIS device's library. A scanned family photo has a 1970 creationDate and a 2026 addedDate — conflating them wrecks any timeline.

**`localIdentifier` is device-local and changes on restore; `PHCloudIdentifier` is stable across devices.** Any long-lived personal archive must store the cloud identifier (via `cloudIdentifierMappings(forLocalIdentifiers:)`) or the entire dataset silently de-references after a device migration.

**PHAssetCollectionType.moment is effectively dead.** Apple stopped populating Moments when the Photos app moved to the Memories model; `fetchMoments` compiles, runs, and returns nothing. Treat empty moment results as expected rather than debugging them.

**Safari Web Extensions are supported on iOS, but Apple supports NONE of the browsing-history APIs** — the `history` permission is accepted in manifest.json and is completely inert. However the `tabs` API IS supported on iOS, so a self-installed Safari Web Extension can observe navigation LIVE (forward-only, from install date) via tabs events and content scripts. That is the only legitimate browsing-behavior proxy on iOS, and it is forward-only by construction — there is no path to existing history.

**A custom keyboard extension with `RequestsOpenAccess = true` is a legitimate, non-hacky keyboard-input capture path for a self-installed app** — it sees text typed into it across all apps, excluding secure-entry fields (UITextField.isSecureTextEntry / SwiftUI SecureField), which iOS force-switches back to the system keyboard. It needs no signed entitlement, only the Info.plist key plus the user toggling "Allow Full Access" in Settings. Keyboard input is therefore NOT flatly impossible — it is impossible to capture *passively*, but capturable if the owner adopts your keyboard.

**Clipboard: the impossibility is about background execution, not permission.** `UIPasteboard.detectPatterns(for:)`/`detectedValues(for:)` classify pasteboard contents WITHOUT reading them and WITHOUT triggering the iOS paste banner — you can learn 'the clipboard currently holds a phone number and a URL' with no user-visible prompt (DetectedValues exposes: probableWebSearch, probableWebURL, number, links, phoneNumbers, emailAddresses, postalAddresses, calendarEvents, flightNumbers, moneyAmounts, shipmentTrackingNumbers). But clipboard POLLING is impossible for a structural reason no permission can fix: iOS grants no arbitrary background execution, so there is no process alive to poll. UIPasteboard.changedNotification only fires for your own app while foregrounded. Both halves matter — most write-ups get one and miss the other.

**Call log: `CXCallObserver` is the real partial proxy and its limits are precise.** It reports live call start/connect/end/hold and direction (CXCall: uuid, isOutgoing, hasConnected, hasEnded, isOnHold) — giving you call COUNT, DIRECTION and DURATION with no entitlement. What it cannot give you: the phone number (never exposed), any historical call log (forward-only from when your observer is registered), and anything at all while your app isn't running. CallDirectory extensions are write-only (you supply blocked/identified numbers; you cannot read them back). So: 'call log' is impossible; 'call metadata going forward, while running' is not.

**Photos People/Faces are NOT in PhotoKit** — there is no public API for the Photos app's face-recognition results or named people. The `.albumSyncedFaces` / `.smartFolderFaces` subtypes are legacy iPhoto-sync artifacts, not the modern People album. The honest proxy is to run **Vision** (VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest / VNGenerateFaceprintRequest and friends) yourself over PHAssets you already have permission to read, and build your own face clustering — fully on-device, no entitlement, just compute.

**Messages/iMessage content is impossible, and the API shape proves it rather than merely implying it.** `MSConversation` — the richest object any third-party code ever gets inside Messages — exposes exactly `selectedMessage` (an MSMessage YOUR OWN extension created), `localParticipantIdentifier` and `remoteParticipantIdentifiers`, and those participant identifiers are **opaque UUIDs that are not resolvable to phone numbers, emails, or contacts**. There is no read surface for message text at any permission or entitlement level. Partial proxies, both weak: an iMessage app extension sees only its own messages; SiriKit INSendMessageIntent donations cover only messages your app sends. The macOS chat.db route has no iOS analogue.

**Mail is impossible with no proxy whatsoever — and the citation is a platform line.** MailKit is **macOS 12.0 only**; it does not exist on iOS in any form. On iOS, MFMailComposeViewController is send-only and returns just a result code, never content. Unlike Messages (which at least has an in-conversation extension point) and Safari (which at least has live tab observation), Mail has no partial read surface of any kind on iOS.

**Other apps' notifications are impossible, and the reason is architectural rather than policy.** UNUserNotificationCenter is per-app by construction — Notification Service and Notification Content extensions only ever see YOUR app's own payloads. There is no iOS equivalent of Android's NotificationListenerService and no entitlement that grants one; app sandboxing means the data never enters your address space. Accessibility-based interception exists on macOS, not iOS. No proxy exists.
